developmentNotes: Native DLL packages run in the Pulse process after explicit enablement.
Resource declarations disclose package capabilities during installation; they do not authorize individual calls or sandbox native code.
The broker retains operation names, request shape, snapshot freshness, task ownership and file-operation confirmation checks.

resourceApi.transport: Native host broker; operation names describe the internal request protocol, not an executable MCP entry.
notes: Opaque file cursors and entries are principal/owner/current-snapshot bound, valid five minutes; no path or claimed caller is accepted.
Settings are persistent per package and use expectedVersion compare-and-swap; null deletes a key.
Audit exposes only this principal session records and does not record request payloads or paths.
operations.get/cancel act only on owned task IDs. Resource discovery does not expose a caller-supplied identity or executable MCP resource tool.
resourceApi.resourceDeclarationPolicy: Installation disclosure only; native code runs in process without per-call permission gates.

stability.prefixTableRule: Append-only struct-prefix evolution (V1 <= V2 <= V3 <= V4): existing fields preserve identical index, name, type, size, and byte offset; new fields append strictly at the tail with monotonically increasing struct size and version.
stability.experimentalSurfaceRule: Opt-in UI surface not yet covered by binary freeze; plugins must handle query_interface returning PULSE_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE or PULSE_ERROR_ABI (C++ std::nullopt fallback) gracefully.

emergencyRevocation.scope: Immediate revocation reserved exclusively for active security vulnerabilities, memory corruption, or host-crashing defects.
